planting.note: Plant in filtered sun or part shade after last frost; mulch and keep soil evenly moist through establishment.

directions: Monrovia released this mophead hydrangea in 2026 to mark its 100th year in business. The ruby-red flowers deepen in color as they age, sometimes shading nearly to black, and rebloom from late spring into fall on a compact, sturdy plant. It prefers filtered sun or partial shade with soil kept consistently moist but never soggy.
sources: Monrovia (monrovia.com) — Centennial Ruby Hydrangea product page

planting.note: Plant corms or divisions in rich, well-drained soil in full to partial sun; water regularly the first season.

directions: This 2026 Monrovia introduction pairs smoky purple-green foliage with bi-color red-and-yellow summer flowers that draw hummingbirds and butterflies. It is a clump-forming perennial that grows from corms, stays compact at under two feet tall, and tolerates drier soil once established. Divide clumps every three to four years in early spring to keep it vigorous.

planting.note: Plant in well-drained soil in full to partial sun; water deeply until established, then drought tolerant.

directions: A new-for-2026 evergreen shrub from Monrovia, Copper Flame Distylium shows off vivid copper-red new growth against dark green mature foliage, with small, inconspicuous red flowers in early spring. It is tough and adaptable, tolerating heat, drought, and clay soils, and is notably resistant to disease, deer, and rabbits. Use it as a hedge or border planting in warm climates.
sources: Monrovia (monrovia.com) — Copper Flame Distylium product page

planting.note: Plant in enriched, loamy, well-drained soil in full sun; water deeply during establishment.

directions: Monrovia selected this low, nearly thornless rose specifically for its pollinator appeal, making it one of its new 2026 Distinctive Selections. Clusters of blush-pink buds open into single white flowers that bloom repeatedly from spring through fall. It stays compact at about two feet tall, suiting mixed perennial beds or low shrub borders.
sources: Monrovia (monrovia.com) — Honey Blush Rose product page

planting.note: Plant in enriched, well-drained soil in partial sun; avoid burying the crown and avoid excess winter moisture.

directions: Set for spring 2026 shipping, this short, mounding coral bells cultivar shows dark cool-green and purple leaves with wavy margins that reveal wine-red undersides as they grow upright. It stays compact at only about seven inches tall, making it suited to containers or the front edge of perennial beds. The herbaceous perennial attracts hummingbirds and pollinators.
sources: Monrovia (monrovia.com) — Balboa Sunset Heuchera product page
